🎙
Opening remarks
by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at a meeting with US Presidential Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and entrepreneur Jared Kushner
(Moscow, November 12, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Putin:
First of all, I would like to thank you and ask you to convey
my thanks to President Trump
for arranging our contacts with the Ukrainian side.
I know we have made progress on at least one front –
the humanitarian one
. There have been
POW exchanges
, and another major step in this direction is now taking shape.
I would also ask you to convey my thanks to the First Lady of the US
Melania Trump
for her active role in addressing
the humanitarian situation
in and around the town of Alyoshki in the Kherson Region
.
We fully appreciate that this would have been impossible without
the support of President Trump’s entire team
, including
the State Department
,
the Department of War
and other agencies, and without your personal involvement.
There was also a suggestion that
we could continue this work
with the involvement of
representatives of the human rights commissioners
of both Russia and Ukraine.
***
❗️
As for how long peace should last and how sound and secure it should be, we too would like it to last
forever
.
We know that the two sides see territorial issues differently.
What matters more to us is the people who live there
– their traditions, their culture and their right to live by their own rules and in keeping with their traditional values.
We know that the Ukrainian side is raising the issue of so-called
“grey zones”
. As I have already said, this will always be a bone of contention.
For us, there is only one line of demarcation – the state border.
That would make things perfectly clear. You are on one side and we are on the other.
As soon as we get drawn into discussions about
“grey zones”
,
each side understands them differently
. Disputes arise immediately, any agreement becomes shaky and
there can be no lasting peace
.
We still hear the Kiev authorities saying that they control this or that area, or that we do not control some other area.
This could go on indefinitely.
Given the weapons in use today, it is no easy matter to go there and see for oneself what is actually happening.
As I mentioned earlier, we worked well together on
humanitarian issues in Alyoshki
.
Let us continue that work together.
There is a town in Donbass called Konstantinovka
. The Ukrainian side considers it part of its strategic line of defence.
Some 400-500 civilians are still there
.
Let us do what we did in Alyoshki
. Let us invite members of the foreign press, including American journalists, as well as the Russian media. Let us entrust this work to
those responsible for human rights
on both sides – the Russian and Ukrainian human rights commissioners.
***
As for the Europeans,
we have always been open to dialogue with Europe. We have never broken off that dialogue.
It was the Europeans who broke off dialogue with Russia.
❌
We have said from the outset that the presence of any foreign troops on Ukrainian territory is absolutely unacceptable to us because we believe it threatens Russia’s security.
Everyone agreed on that in principle. At any rate, that was the understanding at the talks in Istanbul, and until now no one seems to have objected.
The Europeans know this.
Yet what do we hear from them? That as soon as peace is concluded, they will send troops into Ukraine. What does that mean? We have said this before.
We would regard those troops as a legitimate target, which means the war would resume immediately.
It is an unusual way to put the question
, but we would very much like you, gentlemen, and the US administration as a whole to work with your European allies so that they can finally make up their minds.
👉
What do they want in Ukraine – peace or war?
And we are, of course, ready to work with them.

#InMemoryOfDiplomats
▪️
The leadership of the Russian Foreign Ministry and its Department of the North Atlantic are deeply saddened
to report
the sudden passing of Alexander DARCHIEV (1960-2026)
, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Russian Federation to the United States of America and Permanent Observer of the Russian Federation to the Organization of American States in Washington, D.C. He
passed away
on November 11, 2026,
at the age of 66
.
We have lost
a man of wisdom and depth, an outstanding diplomat, historian and scholar of American affairs
who devoted his entire life and career to the service of his country.
Ambassador Darchiev had a keen and perceptive mind
. Those who worked with him knew him for his exceptional professionalism and talent, his deep commitment to his country’s interests, his unwavering principles and his ability to work shoulder to shoulder with his colleagues.
Alexander Darchiev had an exceptional knowledge and understanding of the countries of North America
, where he worked tirelessly throughout his diplomatic career. Moscow consistently sought his views on developments across the continent. His sound judgement and carefully considered assessments earned him a reputation as
one of Russia’s foremost experts on American affairs
.
His natural refinement, subtle sense of humour and personal charm went hand in hand with a quiet determination
. These qualities enabled him, even at the most delicate moments in Russia’s relations with the United States and Canada, to carry out some of the most demanding tasks his country entrusted to him.
Ambassador Darchiev held a range of posts at
the Ministry’s headquarters
and abroad
. He spent much of his career in senior positions at the Russian embassies
in Washington
and
Ottawa
.
He joined the diplomatic service in 1992
after working at the Institute for US and Canadian Studies of the USSR Academy of Sciences, where he defended his dissertation and earned the degree of Candidate of Historical Sciences.
From 2005 to 2010, he served as Minister-Counsellor at the Russian Embassy in the United States. He headed the Foreign Ministry’s North America Department from 2010 to 2014 and served as Russia’s Ambassador to Canada from 2014 to 2020. He again headed the North America Department from 2021 to 2024 and then led the North Atlantic Department from 2024 to 2025.
From March 2025, he served as
Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Russian Federation to the United States of America
and concurrently as
Russia’s Permanent Observer to the Organization of American States
in Washington, D.C.
His many state and ministerial honours
included the Order of Friendship and the Order of Honour, certificates of honour from the President of the Russian Federation and the Russian Foreign Ministry, the Medal for Strengthening Military Cooperation and the Foreign Ministry’s Badge of Distinction.
🕯
We mourn the untimely loss of our mentor and friend. Our heartfelt condolences go out to his family and loved ones.
We will always remember Alexander Darchiev with warmth and affection. His professionalism and vibrant personality will remain with us forever.

#GID

. Official representatives of the Republic of Abkhazia, Georgia, the Republic of South Ossetia, the Russian Federation and the United States of America took part. The UN, the OSCE and the EU co-chaired the talks.
Participants expressed their
shared commitment to continuing work under the GID
, which remain the only forum for rebuilding Tbilisi’s
post-conflict
relations with Sukhum and Tskhinval.
Participants highlighted the continued work of the existing channels for dialogue, including regular rounds of talks, 24-hour hotlines and meetings of
the Incident Prevention and Response Mechanism
(
#IPRM
) in Ergneti on the Georgian-South Ossetian border.
The Russian Side once again stressed
the importance of taking practical steps to ensure lasting security for Abkhazia and South Ossetia
.
☝️
Moscow and its Abkhaz and South Ossetian allies believe that priority should be given to
agreeing on legal guarantees that Tbilisi will not use force against the two sovereign republics
, beginning the process of
delimiting Georgia’s borders
with its neighbours and
resuming IPRM meetings in Gal
on the Georgian-Abkhaz border.
These measures are necessary due to
ongoing threats to the independence of Abkhazia and South Ossetia
. These risks stem both from
radical forces within Georgia
and from some of its closest foreign partners, particularly
NATO member states
that refuse to recognise the realities in the South Caucasus and continue to expand military cooperation with Tbilisi.
By joining the EU’s illegal anti-Russian sanctions,
Switzerland has effectively abandoned its declared neutrality
. With the support of Sukhum and Tskhinval, the Russian Side continued its efforts to build consensus on moving the GID meetings
from Geneva to a genuinely neutral venue acceptable to all participants.
🤝
Participants reached a preliminary agreement to hold
the next round of the GID in March 2027.

📄
Declaration of the Collective Security Council of the Collective Security Treaty Organization
(Moscow, November 11, 2026)
✍️
We, the members of the Collective Security Council of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (
#CSTO
),
reaffirm our unconditional commitment
to the objectives set out in
the Collective Security Treaty
and
the CSTO Charter
–
to create favourable and stable conditions
for the comprehensive development of the member states and
to safeguard
their security, sovereignty and territorial integrity.
We regard closer cooperation within the CSTO as one of our foreign policy priorities.
We intend to take joint steps to further strengthen the collective security system.
We emphasise that the CSTO gives priority
to
political and diplomatic means of resolving and settling conflicts
. Its guiding principles include mutual respect and equality, non-interference in the internal affairs of states and due regard for their legitimate interests.
We note that the international situation is undergoing fundamental change
. A just
#MultipolarWorld
order continues to take shape. As new centres of influence grow stronger, competition is intensifying and new challenges to international security and global stability are emerging.
☝️
Amid continuing turbulence in world politics and international relations,
stable and predictable forms of cooperation between states are particularly valuable
. With its time-tested mechanisms, forces and capabilities,
the CSTO is a cornerstone of a stable architecture of equal and indivisible security in Eurasia
. Building such an architecture serves the fundamental interests of the Member States.
We reaffirm our intention to continue working closely together to create conditions in which
every state on the continent can develop free from the threat of external interference
. In doing so, we are guided by the principle that states and groups of states must not pursue their own security at the expense of others.
🌐
To this end, the CSTO Member States will take part in drafting
the Eurasian Charter of Diversity and Multipolarity in the 21st Century
.
We intend to continue working closely together
to enhance the authority of the United Nations and strengthen its role as the principal instrument for maintaining international security
. We will also work to advance a just
#MultipolarWorld
order founded on
the UN Charter
and the rule of international law, and to promote recognition of the many paths that states take towards progress as an asset to human civilisation.
We express concern at
the growing threats and strategic risks
arising as individual states and countries belonging to other military alliances and coalitions move their military and strategic infrastructure closer to the borders of CSTO member states.
❗️
We emphasise that the deployment of weapons systems that threaten collective security along the perimeter of the CSTO’s area of responsibility is
unacceptable
.
We are ready to expand cooperation between the CSTO and other international organisations
, particularly
the Commonwealth of Independent States
and
the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
, with which we share the task of ensuring stability and security across Eurasia. We welcome the establishment of
permanent channels for cooperation
between the CSTO and
the African Union
to strengthen security and address new challenges and threats.

item.title: 🇷🇺 On November 12, a delegation of Russia’s Federation Council led by its Speaker Valentina Matvienko
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇻🇳 On November 12, a delegation of Russia’s Federation Council led by its Speaker Valentina Matvienko began an official visit to the Socialist Republic of Vietnam. Valentina Matvienko held a meeting with Prime Minister of Vietnam Le Minh Hung. Their talks focused on trade and economic cooperation , including at the regional level, the implementation of joint projects and the development of tourism . 💬 Valentina Matvienko: Our delegation includes regional leaders and representatives of Russian state corporations. The purpose of this official visit is to do everything we can through our Parliament to put into effect the agreements reached by our Leaders and implement the intergovernmental documents our two countries have signed. *** Valentina Matvienko was also received by General Secretary of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Vietnam and President of Vietnam To Lam . The Speaker informed the Vietnamese Leader that President of Russia Vladimir Putin had issued an extensive set of instructions to the Russian Government, ministries, agencies and state corporations covering all the agreements reached by the two countries’ Leaders. 💬 Valentina Matvienko: First of all, I would like to convey warm greetings and best wishes from President of Russia Vladimir Putin. He speaks warmly of his meetings with you and values the special relationship you have built – one marked by a businesslike approach, friendship and trust. #RussiaVietnam

item.content:encoded:

⚡️
Press briefing by the Russian delegation, led by Presidential Aide
Vladimir Medinskiy
, following
the talks in Abu Dhabi
(November 11, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Medinskiy:
First of all, on behalf of the entire Russian delegation,
I would like to thank the leadership of the UAE and Abu Dhabi
for the excellent organisation of the trilateral talks and for creating a friendly, businesslike atmosphere.
***
Answers to media questions:
❓
Question: How did the discussion on shaping Europe’s future security architecture proceed?
💬
Vladimir Medinskiy:
We believe it is right to raise the question of what will happen after the inevitable end of the conflict in Ukraine.
❗️
Russia
has repeatedly raised
the issue of European security architecture and the need to establish a new, comprehensive and fair security system in Europe.
We did so
in 2008
, when we proposed
the relevant draft European Security Treaty
, and
in 2021
, when we sent the relevant documents to NATO, the US and European countries.
But, as the saying goes, it is easier said than done.
Many years have passed, and this issue has finally gained attention,
with a growing recognition that it must be addressed
.
The conflict in Ukraine has shown that
the entire European security system in place since
Yalta
and
Potsdam
functions very poorly
. In essence, the entire body is diseased, and Ukraine is simply where
the abscess has burst
.
With the US Side participating, we exchanged views. We found common ground on some points, but not on others.
This discussion will certainly continue.
☝️
The world needs a new, modern, renewed security system
that is fair and does not come at the expense of individual countries. We will work towards that.
❓
Question: EU representatives were also in Abu Dhabi. Did you speak to them, and are any meetings with them planned?
💬
Vladimir Medinskiy:
We did not speak to them.
We are not quite sure in what capacity they are here
. The talks are being held in the agreed trilateral format.
As for the stance taken by the leadership of a number of European countries, they are, in essence,
collectively deceiving the Ukrainian people
. They finance and supply weapons to one of the warring parties.
In effect, they are contributing to civilian deaths on a massive scale.
We are not quite sure what there is to discuss with them
. We have not received a single peace initiative or a single concrete peace proposal from European countries. Therefore, it is unclear what there is to discuss.
They would do well to learn
, for example,
from the American envoys
when it comes to
common sense, realism and a desire to achieve peace
.
❓
Question: Were humanitarian issues raised during the meeting? In previous rounds held in Turkiye and Switzerland, you managed to reach agreements with the Ukrainians on POW exchanges, for example. Was such an agreement reached in Abu Dhabi?
💬
Vladimir Medinskiy:
We have agreed in principle
on
a new large-scale prisoner exchange
. The specific details will be announced shortly.
❓
Question: How do you assess the role of Steven Witkoff and Jared Kushner, and the Trump administration more broadly, in the rounds of talks? What role do you believe they can play in reaching agreements?
💬
Vladimir Medinskiy:
The US Side played
an active role
in the talks. The role of individuals in history matters here. President Donald Trump’s envoys are certainly
sincere, effective people
and, most importantly,
focused on results
, rather than empty talk.
What matters is not how we assess them, but
how many lives will be saved
through their active mediation efforts.
We are therefore
very grateful
to them as well.
❓
Question: Under what conditions could the Europeans become full participants in the talks? What conditions must they meet to be admitted to the negotiating table?
💬
Vladimir Medinskiy:
I think
as soon as their conscience awakens
, they can become participants in peace talks.
Until then, as I have said,
they are taking part in the collective deception of the Ukrainian people
and are, in effect, complicit in
civilian deaths
.

the Declaration of the CSTO Collective Security Council
.
💬
Vladimir Putin:
My colleagues and I have just held a thorough and productive exchange of views in
a restricted format
on
pressing global and regional security issues
.
We reached
full mutual understanding
on virtually every issue discussed. We reaffirmed our commitment to further joint efforts
to counter acute challenges and threats to collective security
.
I am pleased to note that Council members gave
a positive assessment of the results of
Russia’s CSTO chairmanship in 2026
. Our chairmanship benefited from
the friendly assistance and support
of our colleagues across the Organisation.
🤝
Together, we held more than a hundred events across key areas of cooperation.
We took coordinated steps to promote our common position on the international stage, including at the UN and other multilateral forums.
Our shared approaches
to the current situation in the world and our region, and
our vision of the priorities for the CSTO’s development
, are reflected in
the draft Declaration of the Collective Security Council
, which Russia has proposed adopting at today’s meeting.
As always, considerable attention was paid to improving the operational and combat readiness of the forces and assets within the collective security system
. A series of major joint exercises took place in Belarus, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and, of course, Russia. In particular,
the CSTO Collective Rapid Reaction Forces
successfully held
the Interaction 2026 exercise
in the Chelyabinsk Region alongside
the Centre-2026 strategic command post exercise
.
We also continued our systematic efforts to equip our collective forces with modern weapons and equipment.
I would like to stress that today we are to take
important decisions
on the further development of the CSTO Collective Forces. These concern, among other things, their
aviation component
and the formation of
mobile air defence units for joint military operations
.
Close operational contacts among our security agencies, law enforcement bodies and relevant services
helped strengthen coordination between our countries in combating terrorism, extremism, illicit drugs, drug trafficking and illegal migration. We also closely monitored
the situation in Afghanistan
as part of our efforts to strengthen security along the Organisation’s external borders.
Partnership among CSTO member states in
ensuring biological safety
and
countering the spread of dangerous infections
has gained considerable momentum.
☝️
Next year, 2027, will be particularly significant for our Organisation, marking two anniversaries:
35 years since the signing of
the Collective Security Treaty
and 25 years since
the establishment of the CSTO
.
Our friends in Tajikistan
, who will assume the chairmanship,
therefore face a substantial and demanding task
: both taking stock of our many years of cooperation and defining the strategic prospects for its further development.
Naturally, CSTO Member States will provide their colleagues in Tajikistan with
all the assistance they need
.
